note: Digging yields (Dave 2026-10-21, job 84). A shovel dig gives what the ground at the hole is made of, as shovelfuls: [item, min, max], the number rolled through luck (more when lucky) and counted into the pack by weight like any pick (what does not fit lands on the ground). yield is by the surface material name from data/tables/soils.json; 'rock' is bare rock showing (a stone or two). under: a chance of a second kind from the layer below the topsoil (wet lowland soils lie on clay); gravel and bare rock hide a rare crystal lens (clear quartz, the tier 1 spyglass lens, docs/design/spyglass_design.md). fill is what filling a hole uses up, tried in this order; the fill operation (River start, Ground) calls ServerItems.take_fill(peer, units). A better shovel lifts more: tier_extra adds that many shovelfuls to the top of the roll by the shovel's tier in items.json (wooden 1: none, iron 4: 2, steel 5: 3; tiers by material rank, master s4 item 13). A shovelful weighs 4 to 5 kg (weights.json), so a body carries about nine before it slows. Shovel sizes (Dave 2026-10-22): shovel_sizes by an item's shovel_size (default small): pieces = shovelfuls moved per stroke (1, 4, 8; a dig yields that many times the roll, a Raise stroke takes that many shovelfuls from the pack). The sphere radius grows with the cube root of the pieces, and pace and wear with it. 10 Nov 2026 (coordinator, item_system.md): a salt flat's crust is salt (the same Salt as sea salt), with sand under it. finds: small chances per dig stroke of a thing living in the soil, by surface material: a worm in moist living soils (not sand, gravel, clay or acid peat), one per stroke at most; an item that does not exist yet gives nothing. bog_iron (Sonny s11, 10 Nov 2026): a deposit of iron_ore under fen, marsh, swamp and bog samples, found with any shovel; the rule lives in src/shared/bog_iron.gd. 28 Nov 2026 (coordinator, R-CRAFT-CLAY-DIG, from the crafting chain check: about 100 digs to reach copper was gating): an under row may carry an amount, [item, chance, min, max], rolled like a soil row and times the shovel size's pieces (a two-value row gives 1); clay ground gives 2 to 4 clay and the wet soils' clay layer 2 to 3 (loam and forest humus at 0.7, silt and alluvium at 0.9), so the 52 clay of the way to copper (smelter 24, smithy 10, smoker 6, two pots 12) take about 20 to 30 digs. Dave 19 Nov 2026: it gives its own Bog iron ore (two smelt to one iron ingot), and its stain is seen from seen_m 50 m. Dave 21 Nov 2026: no stain sheet; the ground itself is rust-tinted where the ore lies and goes back to plain peat where it is dug; deposits come in fields of several patches along the wet edge (field_m .. radius_m, src/shared/bog_iron.gd, PROVISIONAL BI-3); a hole dug in fen, marsh, swamp or bog silts back in after refill_game_days (PROVISIONAL BI-4). Dave 28 Nov 2026 (R-RES-DIG-STONES): every shovelful of soil or clay ground is part soil, part clay, part stones: soil and clay grounds (loam, forest humus, silt, alluvium, peat, mud, clay, the default) always bring up one Stone (stone 1..1, plus the shovel tier's extra, times the pieces), taken out of the top of the soil roll (loam soil 1-3 became soil 1-2 and a stone; peat and mud 1-2 became 1 and a stone), so a wooden or stone shovel's shovelful keeps its count (a better shovel's tier_extra tops up both the soil and the stone roll); stony soil gives 1 to 2 stones, never none. Clay is not cut for it (clay ground keeps 2 to 4 clay and gains the stone; the under rows are unchanged), so the way to copper still takes about 20 to 30 digs. Sand, gravel, ash, salt, ice and snow are unchanged. A stone weighs 0.5 kg, a soil 0.1 kg (weights.json), so a loam shovelful now weighs 0.6 to 0.7 kg plus its clay; what does not fit lands at the feet.
